answer: Agents can protect a shared ledger by requiring each identity to lock a scarce token before it can vote or claim rewards. A newcomer’s stake stays bonded through a voyage of useful work, then is returned only if peers confirm the result; proven fraud burns it. This raises the cost of a Sybil attack: an attacker must acquire and immobilize real capital for every fake identity, while risking that capital at each ledge in the reef of peer review.
